clue.text: English fighter about to become one settled abroad

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter aircraft
re is Latin-derived 'concerning', i.e. about

explanation.surface: An English combatant on the point of relocating overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: An émigré is a person who has left their own country to live permanently in another.

clue.text: Develop curiosity without others about island

indicators.note: about says the shortened word goes around the island
without says a word for 'others' is taken away from the word for curiosity

parts.note: interest is curiosity or a wish to know
the rest means the others
Cuba is a Caribbean island

explanation.surface: Someone's inquisitiveness grows, apart from others, concerning an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' leaves INTE, the shortened form of the word for curiosity, and 'about' wraps that round the island.
explanation.definitionFit: To incubate is to nurture or let something grow, as an egg or an idea develops over time.

clue.text: Dress, a number worn by broadcasting executive showing dynamism

parts.note: a get-up is an outfit, a way of dressing

indicators.note: worn by says the executive's letters have the other pieces around them, like clothing

parts.note: DG is Director General, the head of the BBC

explanation.surface: A frock worn by a BBC boss reveals her energetic character.
explanation.walkthrough: The Director General is the head of the BBC, Britain's public broadcaster; 'worn by' means the executive sits inside, so the A and the number go around him.
explanation.definitionFit: Get-up-and-go is an idiom for energy and enthusiasm, the same drive as dynamism.

clue.text: Favour element forgoing resistance

indicators.note: forgoing says the element gives up the letter for resistance

parts.note: boron is a chemical element
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A preferred chemical element that no longer resists.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a favour or blessing granted to someone.

clue.text: Support among fans with minute gone in game

parts.note: to back is to support

indicators.note: gone in says the letter for minute is placed inside the rearranged letters
fans as a verb, spreading out, signals the letters of among are rearranged

explanation.surface: Backing amid supporters, with a minute to go in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fans' looks like the supporters but is the anagram signal: AMONG becomes GAMON, and 'gone in' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game for two played with dice and counters.

clue.text: Exam or lesson in which master is deficient

indicators.note: is deficient says the lesson word lacks the letter for master

parts.note: a moral is the lesson a story teaches
M is the abbreviation for master, as in an MA degree

explanation.surface: A test, or a class where the teacher falls short.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, as in a language test.

clue.text: Equipment mostly put on car in Italian port

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter of the equipment word is dropped

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: Most of the kit is loaded onto a car in an Italian harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' says the shortened equipment word comes before the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a resort and port on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Grotesque sort of royal egg, scrambled

indicators.note: scrambled, as eggs are, says the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A bizarre kind of regal egg, cooked scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotesque is a carved fantastical figure, and a gargoyle is a carved grotesque spout on a building.

clue.text: Maine's not mistaken for another state

indicators.note: mistaken says the letters are taken wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Maine is confused with a different US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another state' works because Maine is itself a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is a US state in the upper Midwest, another of the fifty besides Maine.

clue.text: Characteristic principally lacking with a dish from India

indicators.note: principally lacking says the word loses its first, principal letter

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic

explanation.surface: An Indian dish missing a key feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is a yoghurt side dish of Indian cuisine, often with cucumber.

clue.text: Good promise falling short in artist

indicators.note: falling short says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to augur is to promise or portend

explanation.surface: Potential that was not fulfilled in a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Gauguin was a French post-impressionist painter known for his Tahiti works.

clue.text: Piece of skill in gambling producing large financial gain

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bit of gambling skill brings in a big win.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'producing' into the definition; it is the link, since the noun means a large financial gain, not producing one.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a killing is an idiom for a big, quick profit.

clue.text: Revered figure loses head for a period

indicators.note: loses head says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Hera was the queen of the Greek gods, a revered figure

explanation.surface: An idolised person is decapitated for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a distinct span of historical time.

clue.text: It could be represented in amiable type (not half)

definitions.text: It could be represented in amiable type (not half)

indicators.note: could be represented says the letters may be presented in another order
not half says only the first half of the word is used

explanation.surface: Agreeableness might be shown by a pleasant sort of person, or not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: TY is the first half of 'type'; it joins IN and AMIABLE in the anagram, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenability is willingness to comply, a trait an amiable type of person would show.

clue.text: Figures on register required for returns?

definitions.text: Figures on register required for returns?

parts.words: Figures on register required for returns?
parts.note: people listed on the voters' roll are needed to produce election returns, the results declared

explanation.surface: Numbers in a ledger needed for tax returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' and 'returns' suggest accounts; here they are people on the electoral register and election results.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the body of people entitled to vote, recorded on the electoral register.

clue.text: Cheer Latin rogue out of difficulty

indicators.note: rogue, behaving wildly, says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rowdy Latin chant celebrates escaping trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the clear is an idiom for being free of danger, suspicion or trouble.

clue.text: Fear day before study

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: Anxiety on the day before an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great apprehension, a deep fear of what is coming.

clue.text: Lift for police detaining ungentlemanly sort after appeal that's instructive

indicators.note: in a down answer, a lift reads the letters upward, from bottom to top
detaining says the police letters hold the other pieces inside

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department

indicators.note: after says the cad follows the appeal word

parts.note: it is sex appeal
a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably

explanation.surface: An elevator for officers holding a bounder after a plea teaches a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: C(IT CAD)ID, read upwards, gives the answer; CID is Britain's plain-clothes detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactic writing or speech is designed to teach or moralise.

clue.text: Tree guide lacking introduction

indicators.note: lacking introduction says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: the helm is what steers or guides a ship

explanation.surface: A tree guidebook missing its preface.
explanation.definitionFit: The elm is a large deciduous tree of the genus Ulmus.

clue.text: Sample discrimination

definitions.meaning: to sample food is to try a little of it
the ability to judge what is fine or of quality, as in good judgement in art

explanation.surface: Try out discernment.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: trying a mouthful, and refined judgement in matters of style.

clue.text: Model getting drunk? Wait patiently

parts.note: to sit for an artist is to model
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Is the model drunk? Stay where you are and be patient.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit tight is an idiom for staying put and waiting rather than acting.

clue.text: Stop discordant tune in club first

indicators.note: first says the club word comes at the front

parts.note: a disco is a nightclub

indicators.note: discordant, out of harmony, says the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Halt the jarring melody in the nightclub first.
explanation.definitionFit: To discontinue something is to stop doing or providing it.

clue.text: Ring from Cornish area I have put on top of locker

parts.note: Cornwall is in the south-west of England, abbreviated SW

indicators.note: top of says only the first letter of locker is used

explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' places L at the bottom of this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A swivel is a ring or link turning on a pin, letting attached parts rotate.

clue.text: Recall deeply personal pull

indicators.note: recall, calling back, says the letters run backwards

parts.note: a gut feeling is deeply personal, instinctive

explanation.surface: Remember a very private attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: To tug is to pull hard or sharply.

clue.text: Discussion of inexperienced novelist

indicators.note: discussion is talk, so the word is heard spoken

parts.note: green means new and inexperienced

explanation.surface: Talk about an untried writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was an English novelist, author of Brighton Rock.

clue.text: College joint for one that's cheerful

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body
per means for each, for one

explanation.surface: A college hip-hop spot for someone who's happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chipper is informal for lively and in good spirits.

clue.text: Secretary facing outwardly tough course

parts.note: a PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

indicators.note: outwardly says only the outside letters of the word are used

explanation.surface: An assistant facing a tough course, on the outside.

clue.text: Clash with daughter enthralled by dog

indicators.note: enthralled by says the daughter is held within the dog

parts.note: a collie is a sheepdog breed

explanation.surface: A girl captivated by her pet dog has a row.

clue.text: Betray on radio tight-knit group

indicators.note: on radio means heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: to sell someone out is to betray them

explanation.surface: Betray a close circle on the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell is a small close group within a larger organisation, as of activists or spies.

clue.text: Clumsy painter awkwardly dropping a roller initially

indicators.note: awkwardly says the letters are muddled, and dropping says some are taken out first
initially says only the first letter of roller is used

explanation.surface: A clumsy decorator fumbles his roller at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A and R out of PAINTER to leave PINTE, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill, awkward and incompetent.

clue.text: Time a woman interrupts endlessly extended debate

indicators.note: interrupts says the woman breaks into the other word
endlessly says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: long means extended
Kath is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman keeps breaking into an endless, drawn-out argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves LON, and the woman's name goes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A talkathon is a long-drawn-out debate or discussion.
